questions.question:
N items are stored in a sorted doubly linked list. For a delete operation, a pointer is provided to the record to be deleted. For a decrease-key operation, a pointer is provided to the record on which the operation is to be performed.
An algorithm performs the following operations on the list in this order: [latex]\Theta(N) \; delete [/latex] , [latex] O(logN) \; insert [/latex], [latex] O(logN) \; find [/latex], and [latex] \Theta(N) \; decrease-key[/latex]. What is the time complexity of all these operations put together?
questions.explanation:
In a sorted doubly linked list (pointers given for delete and decrease-key):
- delete: [latex]O(1)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(N)[/latex] in total
- insert: find the position, [latex]O(N)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N\log N)[/latex]
- find: [latex]O(N)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N\log N)[/latex]
- decrease-key: the node may have to move back towards the front, [latex]O(N)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N^2)[/latex]

Total = [latex]O(N^2)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]O(N^2)[/latex]

questions.question:
Suppose the values 10, -4, 15, 30, 20, 5, 60, 19 are inserted in that order into an initially empty binary search tree. Let [latex]T [/latex] be the resulting binary search tree.  
The number of edges in the path from the node containing 19 to the root node of [latex]T [/latex] is ___________. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanation:
Insert each value into the BST, always going left for smaller and right for larger than the current node:

[latex]10[/latex] (root) → [latex]-4[/latex] (left of [latex]10[/latex]) → [latex]15[/latex] (right of [latex]10[/latex]) → [latex]30[/latex] (right of [latex]15[/latex]) → [latex]20[/latex] (left of [latex]30[/latex]) → [latex]5[/latex] (right of [latex]-4[/latex]) → [latex]60[/latex] (right of [latex]30[/latex]) → [latex]19[/latex] (left of [latex]20[/latex]).

Path from [latex]19[/latex] up to the root: [latex]19\to20\to30\to15\to10[/latex], which is [latex]4[/latex] edges.

Answer: 4

questions.question:
Suppose we are given [latex]n[/latex] keys, [latex]m[/latex] hash table slots, and two simple uniform hash functions [latex]h_1[/latex] and [latex]h_2[/latex]. Further suppose our hashing scheme uses [latex]h_1[/latex] for the odd keys
and [latex]h_2[/latex] for the even keys. What is the expected number of keys in a slot?
questions.explanation:
Both [latex]h_1[/latex] and [latex]h_2[/latex] are simple uniform hash functions, so every key (odd or even) lands in any given slot with probability [latex]\frac{1}{m}[/latex].

Expected keys in a slot [latex]=n\times\frac{1}{m}=\frac{n}{m}[/latex] (which hash function is used does not matter).

Answer: [latex]\frac{n}{m}[/latex]

questions.question:
The number of ways in which the numbers 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 can be inserted in an empty binary search tree, such that the resulting tree has height 6, is _____.

[latex]2^6=64[/latex]

questions.question:
A complete binary min-heap is made by including each integer in [1,1023] exactly once. The depth of a node in the heap is the length of the path from the root of the heap to that node. Thus, the root is at depth 0. The maximum depth at which integer 9 can appear is_____.
.
questions.explanation:
In a min-heap every ancestor of 9 must be smaller than 9. Only 1-8 are smaller, so 9 can have at most 8 ancestors [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] depth at most 8. This is possible: put 1, 2, [latex]\ldots[/latex], 8, 9 down one path (the heap of 1023 nodes has depths 0-9).

Answer: 8

questions.question:
Let Q denote a queue containing sixteen numbers and S be an empty stack. Head(Q) returns the element at the head of the queue Q without removing it from Q. Similarly Top(S) returns the element at the top of S without removing it from S. Consider the algorithm given below.

The maximum possible number of iterations of the while loop in the algorithm is_________.
questions.explanation:
The loop keeps the stack in sorted order, sending larger stack tops back to the queue. The worst case is when the queue is in decreasing order: every element has to be cycled between the stack and the queue many times.

For n elements the worst case is [latex]n^2[/latex] iterations (check n = 2 with queue [2, 1]: 4 iterations). For n = 16: [latex]16^2=256[/latex].

Answer: 256
